Figure 4: Method-level overview of M2E-Point and its optional IMU-conditioned variant. The event branch samples [x, y, t, p] points, extracts local event features with EdgeConv, and aggregates them into a global packet feature. The optional IMU-conditioned variant modulates the global feature via FiLM. Local features and the packet feature are fused for event-level foreground scoring, and DBSCAN converts predicted foreground clusters into a detection-style box.

Figure 1: Teaser of the M2E-UAV onboard motion-on-motion setting. Left: schematic and real data-collection scene in which a carrier UAV observes a tiny target UAV. Right: actual onboard event-camera data under sensor ego-motion, where background structures induce dense event clutter around sparse target evidence.

Figure 2: M2E-UAV data collection and benchmark construction. The top row shows the onboard sensing platform, including the carrier UAV, event camera, IMU, vibration-damping mount, and STM32-based trigger synchronization board. The bottom diagram summarizes how synchronized event and IMU streams are organized into matched event-IMU packets and paired with event-level UAV/background labels for benchmark evaluation. The packet construction and label lifting steps are detailed in Sections 3.2 and 3.4.
Table 6: Implementation details used for the validation-stage M2E-Point + IMU result.

Figure 5: Detailed packet-level visualization of point-level prediction and clustering. Foregroundscore colors indicate the model-estimated UAV foreground probability for each sampled event, from low-score blue/green points to medium-score yellow points and high-score red/purple points. In the DBSCAN view, light gray points are sampled inference points, dark gray or black points are unclustered foreground candidates, colored points denote DBSCAN clusters, and the highlighted cluster is selected as the target cluster. The lower row zooms into the tiny-UAV region to show sparse target evidence and nearby clutter.
